`sun logs` fails for `fn` (CronJob) services — checks for Deployment resource only

**Description:** `cli/sun/bin/cmd_logs.ml` checks whether a `Deployment` resource named `<service>` exists in the target namespace before streaming (`kubectl get deployment/<name> -n <ns>`). Services generated by `sun new fn` are rendered as `CronJob` resources (not `Deployment`) in `cli/sun/lib/sun_cli_deployment_plan.ml`. Running `sun logs billing/invoice` for a deployed fn service always fails with "Service billing/invoice not found in namespace…" even when the CronJob exists. Neither `sun logs --help`, `README.md`, nor `TUTORIAL.md` documents this limitation. The CLI reference table shows `sun logs <service>` generically without any caveat about fn services.

**Impact:** An engineer who deploys a scheduled function with `sun new fn` and follows the documented Day-2 operations path by running `sun logs billing/invoice` will receive a confusing "not found" error with no actionable guidance. They must resort to `kubectl logs -n <ns> job/<name>-<hash>` directly — exactly the kind of kubectl knowledge the platform promise is designed to eliminate.

**Remediation:** Two options, do one or both: (A) Fix `cli/sun/bin/cmd_logs.ml`: when `kubectl get deployment/<name>` fails, check for a CronJob (`kubectl get cronjob/<name> -n <ns>`). If found, find the most recent Job pod (`kubectl get pods -n <ns> -l job-name=<name> --sort-by=.status.startTime`) and tail its logs. (B) Until (A) is done, add a clear fallback message: "billing/invoice is a scheduled function (CronJob) — use: kubectl logs -n <ns> job/<name>-<hash>". Also add a note to `README.md` §"Streaming logs" and the CLI reference table documenting the fn limitation.
